Arizona investigating OpenAI, other firms over possible rogue agents OpenAI faces a criminal investigation in Arizona amid concerns over rogue AI agents and their potential access to banking systems

OpenAI faces a criminal investigation in Arizona amid concerns over rogue AI agents and their potential access to banking systems.

Reuters 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 20 2026 | 12:12 AM IST

By David Thomas   The state of Arizona ??has opened a criminal investigation into  OpenAI and other AI companies relating to the "apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents," ??Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes said Wednesday.   A criminal investigation does not necessarily mean charges will be brought. Mayes said her office was investigating whether Arizona state law was being violated  on an ongoing basis.   "The  state of Arizona is very worried about this, and we  are looking at it from multiple angles," Mayes told a press conference in Chicago.   Mayes declined to identify the other companies her office was investigating. She said her office had been in contact with Arizona banks,  but declined to name them or give their responses.

A spokesperson for OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.   Also Read

Irdai chief flags consumer data grab before insurance price discovery

Anthropic raises $81 bn, set to secure $1.8 trn valuation in Nasdaq debut

India can leverage AI in aerospace, defence, space sectors: TiE Bangalore

AI errors could pose cascading risks to financial institutions: SBI chief

Java security flaw explained: Why CISA, CERT-In urge urgent software update

The banking  industry has become increasingly concerned that sophisticated AI agents could harm the banking system and the institutions trusted to hold people's wealth. Reuters reported last month that major US banks have  been blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside customer accounts and making transactions.   Mayes' comments come two days ??after California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI for allegedly developing  a dangerous product without adequate safety procedures or oversight after reports that its AI models had carried out cyberattacks independently.   OpenAI  did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on that lawsuit, but the company has acknowledged a general need for more transparency around rogue AI behavior and said it was reinforcing its safeguards. On September 16, the company published a new framework for disclosing such incidents, saying it would err on the side of transparency "even when significance is uncertain."

item.title: Grand Theft Auto 6: New Vice City, record viewership, and global frenzy
item.description: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto brings a new story and a more detailed Vice City, drawing record livestream audiences, and glowing reviews, even as players report early technical glitches ...
item.dc:creator: Harsh Shivam
item.content:encoded: More than a decade after Grand Theft Auto V, Rockstar Games has release a new chapter called the Grand Theft Auto 6, bringing players back to Vice City in a new open-world adventure centred on two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. The launch has drawn millions of viewers to gaming livestreams, received near-perfect scores from critics and attracted attention beyond the gaming community. While some players have reported glitches and technical issues, the initial response suggests that GTA 6 has made a strong start. Here is a look at the gameplay experience and how the game has been received globally.First impression: A different kind of GTA experienceGTA 6 does not take long to establish its setting or introduce the relationship at the centre of its story. The opening begins in Vice City, two years before the main events. Jason Duval finds himself in a tense encounter with Lucia Caminos, who confronts him over a car. The situation escalates, bringing the police into the picture and forcing the two to work together to get away.Screenshot from GTA 6 opening sequenceThe sequence then moves into a stylised introduction, with illustrations, music and glimpses of Vice City's nightlife, beaches and neon-lit skyline. It also offers an early look at the growing relationship between the two protagonists before revealing that Lucia is in prison. The story subsequently moves forward to nine months before the opening events, setting up the circumstances in which the main narrative begins. Also Read | Get GTA 6 in minutes: Blinkit rolls out quick delivery in 11 cities The opening is relatively brief, but it establishes an important difference from GTA V. While the earlier game introduced three protagonists whose individual stories eventually converged, GTA 6 builds its narrative around a partnership. Jason and Lucia are not simply two characters players can switch between. Their relationship, conversations and shared criminal pursuits are central to the experience.Vice City in GTA 6 (Screenshot)The early part of the game takes a little time to build momentum. Rather than immediately moving into elaborate heists, it introduces the characters' circumstances and their connections with people in Leonida's criminal underworld. The initial jobs help establish how the pair operate together and provide a gradual introduction to the game's world and mechanics. The change in emphasis is noticeable when compared with GTA V. The earlier game frequently moved between Michael, Franklin and Trevor, using their contrasting personalities and criminal activities to drive the story. GTA 6 is more invested in the dynamic between Jason and Lucia. Their conversations during drives, time spent together away from missions and reactions to events give the narrative a more personal dimension. ALSO READ: GTA 6 India launch: First impressions, prices, editions and download sizeA more detailed world to exploreThe biggest early impression comes from the world itself. Vice City and the wider Leonida setting are designed to feel occupied even when players are not following a mission. Pedestrians have their own conversations and reactions, traffic fills the roads, and unexpected incidents can interrupt an otherwise routine journey. The level of environmental detail is particularly noticeable. The game uses lighting, reflections, weather and character animations to make locations feel more lived-in. Vice City's neon-lit streets and nightlife offer a different atmosphere from its coastal surroundings, while the wider state includes rural areas, waterways and smaller settlements.Screenshot from GTA 6 Chapter 1This is also where GTA 6 appears to move beyond the approach taken in GTA V. The earlier game offered a large and varied map, but the new instalment puts greater emphasis on activity and detail within individual locations. There are also small environmental touches, incidental encounters and everyday activities that can keep players occupied outside the main story. There is also a contrast between the game's criminal missions and the ordinary activities available to Jason and Lucia. Alongside robberies, shootouts and police pursuits, players can spend time fishing, hunting, racing, visiting gyms and exploring the city. The game moves between action-heavy sequences and quieter moments involving everyday activities, giving the relationship between the two protagonists more room to develop. The visual presentation is another noticeable step forward. The city looks different depending on the time of day, while rain, reflections and changing light add detail to roads, vehicles and buildings. Character models and animations are also more detailed, with the behaviour of pedestrians contributing to the sense of activity around the player.Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos in GTA 6 (Screenshot)The controls can feel cumbersome at times, and the campaign takes a while to pick up pace. The opening chapters spend considerable time introducing the characters, their circumstances and the game's mechanics. For players expecting the pace of GTA V's more explosive missions from the outset, GTA 6 may require some patience. But its early hours make clear that Rockstar is attempting more than a visual upgrade to the previous game. The focus on Jason and Lucia, the more involved world and the contrast between criminal activity and everyday life give GTA 6 a different narrative and gameplay rhythm.GTA 6 launch draws record global audienceThe scale of GTA 6's launch became evident within hours of its global rollout. Players across markets began streaming their first experiences of Vice City, while gaming audiences tuned in to watch creators explore the game and share their reactions. According to livestreaming analytics platform Streams Charts, GTA 6 attracted more than 7.18 million concurrent viewers across Twitch, YouTube and Kick during its initial launch period. The figure made it the biggest video game launch on livestreaming platforms tracked by the firm. On Twitch alone, the game crossed 3.29 million concurrent viewers, surpassing the platform's previous record for a game category, held by Fortnite. The launch also drew large audiences to individual gaming channels. Spanish streamer Rubius attracted around 311,000 concurrent viewers within an hour of starting his broadcast, according to Twitch. Indian gaming creator Mythpat was among the leading streamers globally, recording a peak audience of more than 125,000 viewers, according to Streams Charts.ALSO READ: Grand Theft Auto VI wins rave reviews as gamers return to Vice CityThe commercial response has been similarly significant. Analytics firm Sensor Tower estimated that GTA 6 had sold more than 17 million copies, generating over $1.65 billion in revenue by November 19. These are third-party estimates and have not been independently confirmed by Rockstar Games. The figures nevertheless indicate the scale of the game's initial demand. The launch has also extended beyond gaming communities. In India, Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared social media content inspired by the Grand Theft Auto franchise on November 19. Consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off to mark the release, encouraging them to spend the day playing the game. Logging off to lock in ???? https://t.co/0Afoc3juIN— Miami HEAT (@MiamiHEAT) November 19, 2026In Miami, the NBA's Miami Heat marked the occasion with a Vice City-themed match against the Milwaukee Bucks. The court and stadium featured the game's familiar neon pink and blue colours, reflecting the cultural reach of a release that has extended beyond the video game industry. The response has also been visible at gaming events and launch gatherings, with players in cities such as London and Sydney attending midnight celebrations.Critics give GTA 6 near-perfect reviewsThe early critical reception has been overwhelmingly positive. GTA 6 received a Metascore of 99 out of 100 on review aggregator Metacritic, placing it alongside Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the same score since 1998. The aggregate score is subject to change as more reviews are added. Several prominent gaming publications awarded the title their highest ratings. IGN gave it 10 out of 10, with reviewer Luke Reilly describing it as the single most impressive video game he had played. The Guardian, Eurogamer and GamesRadar+ awarded it five stars, while GameSpot and Game Informer also gave it perfect scores. The reviews have particularly highlighted the detail in Leonida's open world and the relationship between Jason and Lucia. The Guardian's Keza MacDonald noted that the relationship between the two protagonists gave the narrative an emotional dimension that was not necessarily expected from the franchise. Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier also described the game as a masterpiece. The Washington Post awarded the game four stars, praising its portrayal of human behaviour and the interactions between its non-playable characters. While the early reviews have been largely positive, some critics have pointed to aspects such as the controls and the pacing of certain sections.Players report glitches and technical issuesThe launch has not been entirely free of technical problems. While the early critical response has been positive, some players and gaming streamers have reported glitches, crashes and unexpected behaviour during their initial sessions. Discussions on gaming forums and social media have included reports of players getting stuck on loading screens, crashes during the opening missions, audio stuttering and occasional problems with character animations. Some PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S users have also reported issues with graphics rendering and gameplay progression. Several clips showing unexpected in-game behaviour have circulated among gaming communities, adding to the discussion around the game's technical performance. However, these reports vary across platforms and individual player experiences, and there is not yet sufficient evidence to suggest a widespread technical failure. Such problems are not uncommon when a large open-world game reaches millions of players. Even after extensive testing, certain glitches can emerge only when a much larger number of users begin interacting with the game across different hardware configurations and gameplay situations. For Rockstar, the immediate challenge will be addressing recurring issues through patches and updates.

Asian stocks rise after Anthropic IPO pricing sets stage for record debut Japan's Nikkei rose 1% in early trading while Nasdaq futures gained 1% and S&P futures were 0.6% higher after Anthropic said the IPO was priced at $83 apiece, above its previously targeted range

Markets mostly shrugged off a strong forecast from chipmaker Nvidia this week as uncertainty caused by CEO Jensen Huang's departure last week rattled investors | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters SINGAPORE 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 19 2026 | 8:50 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Asian equities and US stock futures rose on Thursday after Claude chatbot maker Anthropic scored the biggest IPO ever with an $81 billion offering ahead of its market debut in a test for the AI trade that has been under pressure in recent weeks. Japan's Nikkei rose 1% in early trading while Nasdaq futures gained 1% and S&P futures were 0.6% higher after Anthropic said the IPO was priced at $83 apiece, above its previously targeted range. On a fully diluted basis, the IPO values Anthropic, the first major frontier AI model developer to go public, at about $1.5 trillion and its first-day trading will be scrutinised to gauge investor sentiment on the technology.

Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, said it was going to be a huge test for the markets and it looked poised to be a really bullish listing. "I don't think it's necessarily going to assuage all the fears about AI. I think much of that boils down to future investment growth ... However, if the stock trades the way it looks like it will, it might calm the market a bit." Also Read

Stock Market Close: Sensex snaps 3-day winning run, ends 319 pts lower; Nifty at 25,144; VIX down 7%

Asian stocks fragile, Nvidia plummets as board to decide CEO's fate

Investor confidence in AI has been shaken in the past few weeks on worries about the profitability of the technology and the massive debt needed to fund and build AI infrastructure.

Markets mostly shrugged off a strong forecast from chipmaker Nvidia this week as uncertainty caused by CEO Jensen Huang's departure last week rattled investors. The company's board dismissed the idea of rehiring Huang. The market mood remained fragile with South Korea's Kospi flat while Taiwan stocks were 1% lower. That left MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan down 0.3%, set for a decline of over 4% for the week. In currencies, the dollar was on the front foot as hawkish comments from US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller bolstered expectations of an interest rate hike in December. The euro was at $1.0978, hovering near its lowest since April 2025. The Japanese yen was at 157.42 per US dollar and sterling fetched $1.31515.

Waller said on CNBC that if the central bank wanted to get inflation down it needed to take more "aggressive action" either through a half-point increase at the December meeting, or by using the post-meeting statement to set market expectations for further hikes. The comments come after hotter-than-expected inflation data last week, leaving markets bracing for a rate hike. Traders are pricing in a 90% chance of a 25 basis points hike next month, the CME FedWatch tool showed. "More hawkish Fed pricing has so far offset weakness in technology stocks, keeping the USD supported," OCBC strategists said in a note. "Persistent inflation, further Fed tightening and elevated US yields suggest it is still too early to bet against the USD."

In commodities, oil prices remained under pressure as the growing view that the oil market is turning to a surplus weighed. Brent crude futures were 0.58% lower at $91.47 a barrel, set for a third straight weekly decline.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: DIIs sell ₹55K cr in Nov amid record FII inflows: Tactical or behavioural?
item.description: Amid the sustained inflows in the mutual funds, it's unlikely that DIIs will remain net sellers for long, believe analysts.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / News / DIIs sell ₹55K cr in Nov amid record FII inflows: Tactical or behavioural?

DIIs sell ₹55K cr in Nov amid record FII inflows: Tactical or behavioural? Amid the sustained inflows in the mutual funds, it's unlikely that DIIs will remain net sellers for long, believe analysts.

DIIs, Stock markets. Photo: iStock

Saloni Goel New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 19 2026 | 7:32 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) have adopted a sell-on-rise strategy as a recovery plays out on Dalal Street. Nifty 50 is up over 9 per cent so far in November, and DIIs have been net sellers in 12 out of 13 trading sessions this month in the cash market, selling stocks worth ₹55,570 crore.   This is in contrast to the renewed interest shown by the foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), as they have remained net buyers mostly all through this month, ploughing in a record 94,229 crore in Indian stocks via the cash market, according to data available on exchanges.

Also Read

Stock Market LIVE: GIFT Nifty signals negative open; most Asian markets fall; Brent crude tops $92

Stocks to watch: Dalmia Bharat, Equitas SFB, PSBs, Tata Motors, SBI Funds

Record FPI buying may leave Dec flows muted; correction likely: Analysts

Shifting trends: Largecap funds returned 9.8% in Oct, smallcaps just 0.7%

This tug of war between FIIs and DIIs has been the story of Indian markets, as visible from the graph below.

While DIIs had been net buyers on Dalal Street in the first 10 months of the year, pumping in $74,695 million till October, FIIs pulled out $30,814 million, as per an Edelweiss Mutual Fund report.   Source: Bloomberg | Data as on 30th Oct 2026.

The divergent behaviour is very rational, said Dr VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments, because the DIIs have been buying when the FIIs have been sustained sellers; they are sitting on big profits, and it is perfectly rational on their part to book some profits.   Highlighting a more behavioural aspect, apart from profit-taking by DIIs, Deven Choksey, MD of DRChoksey Finserv, said that DIIs have been acting like investors and FIIs have been following a trading approach.

"DIIs bought at lower levels and sold at higher levels. They are following the investment theory: buy, hold and sell. FPIs are following the trading theory. That's where I think they are different in the current situation," he noted.   The complete reversal of the FII stance is being supported by the better-than-expected Q2 results. Domestic brokerage Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) said that all market-cap categories delivered higher-than-estimated earnings growth.   Moreover, the rupee has been steadily appreciating amid weakness in crude oil prices . The domestic unit has appreciated 1.58 per cent so far in November, its biggest monthly rise since March 2025, when it gained 2.39 per cent.

Volatility in other markets like South Korea, Taiwan and Japan, and improving fundamentals in India, have supported this rally, Vijayakumar added.   CHECK Stock Market LIVE Updates Will DIIs step in if FIIs turn sellers again? Amid the sustained inflows in the mutual funds, it's unlikely that DIIs will remain net sellers for long.   October witnessed equity mutual fund inflows of ₹32,994 crore, alongside SIP contributions of ₹32,160 crore, reflecting the continued strength of domestic savings.   Vijayakumar noted that DIIs will have to deploy the funds, and they cannot go on selling as the FIIs did.   Importantly, this selling also does not indicate weakening domestic investor participation, observed experts.

"We expect DIIs to resume selective buying if FIIs turn net sellers again, particularly when attractive valuations emerge. However, domestic institutions are increasingly valuation-conscious, and their support will depend on earnings visibility, market corrections and global risk sentiment," said Ventura's head of research Vinit Bolinjkar.   He noted that domestic institutions are utilising the improved market liquidity and rally to book profits, rebalance portfolios and maintain their targeted equity allocations.   Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.
